title: Derived telemetry retention, aliasing, and provenance export for metrics and derived request signals
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Redwood currently has strong retention controls for raw requests (prompts/responses) and request logs, but derived telemetry and aggregated metrics (per-route latency histograms, sampled embeddings statistics, model-stage event counts) lack a consistent, auditable lifecycle. Teams need the ability to: 1) apply tenant-aware TTLs to derived metrics without breaking dashboards, 2) alias or pseudonymize keys that could re-identify users before long-term storage, and 3) produce tamper-evident provenance exports (evidence bundles) that tie derived signals back to the raw request material for compliance and eDiscovery.

Goal: Ship a per-tenant "derived-telemetry" retention controller that supports aliasing profiles, time-to-live policies, on-demand evidence exports for a specified time range, and provenance metadata (hash chains + signing) so compliance teams can prove what was retained and why. This ticket covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, migration UX, and dependency coordination with infra and runtime teams.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant TTLs for derived telemetry can be configured in the Console with granular scopes: route, model, aggregation-window (5m/1h/1d)
Alias profiles (one-way pseudonymization) can be applied to identity-like keys in derived signals prior to archival and are reversible only for eDiscovery with an HSM-backed key unblock flow
Evidence export UI/API can generate a signed provenance bundle that includes: list of derived buckets, hash-chain linking to raw request IDs, retention policy snapshots, and export manifest

On-demand evidence export completes within 2 hours for up to 30 days of high-cardinality derived telemetry for Dedicated and Private customers (hosted target is 6 hours), with progress and cost estimate in the UI
Retention simulator shows estimated storage delta and dashboard fidelity impact for proposed derived-telemetry TTLs
All new storage paths for derived telemetry have automated integrity checks and periodic attestations for tamper evidence
Security review sign-off obtained and KMS/HSM integration validated for key material used in alias reversal during eDiscovery
notes: Key constraints discovered in scoping: (a) aggregations live in multiple backends (ClickHouse for high-cardinality, Influx/Prometheus for time-series); (b) aliasing must be consistent across pipelines to avoid fragmenting metrics; (c) provenance must not leak PII in export manifests. We will prototype a lightweight provenance manifest format (JSONL+signed metadata) and iterate with infra. Refer to incident postmortem INC-2024-11 where a partial retention misconfiguration caused 7-day metric gaps — that influenced the simulation requirements.
decisions: Use an abstraction layer (derived-telemetry-controller) that emits lifecycle metadata to the central retention service instead of embedding TTLs in every backend

Alias profiles will be defined centrally with named profiles (e.g., 'hash256-salt-shared', 'pepperable-pseudonym') and assigned per-tenant; reversible aliasing requires documented eDiscovery flow and HSM gating
Evidence bundles will use SHA-256 hash chains and be signed by a rotation-aware service key stored in KMS; the bundle format will be versioned starting at v1
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement controller and aliasing for a small set of non-PII derived metrics in staging; expose simulator and Console preview. Phase 2 (beta): onboard three pilot tenants (one Hosted, one Dedicated, one Private) with monitoring of dashboard fidelity and storage delta. Phase 3 (GA): enable UI rollout, add on-demand evidence export, document eDiscovery procedures, and train Customer Success. Rollback path: controller can set TTL to 'inherit' which returns to legacy behavior; aliasing is reversible only via HSM unseal which requires an ops-level control; ensure default for existing tenants is zero-change unless they opt-in.
migration_strategy: Backfill plan: run a one-time pass that annotates existing derived telemetry records with provenance metadata (source_request_id, aggregation_window, retention_profile); this will be throttled by tenant and off-peak. For ClickHouse tables we will add materialized columns for alias_key and provenance_hash; a schema migration plan and read-path compatibility layer will be coordinated with ENG. Communication: 2-week notice, pre-flight simulator run for each tenant, and optional dry-run export for auditing teams.
api_changes: Retention Admin API additions: POST /tenants/{id}/derived-retention (policy payload), GET /tenants/{id}/derived-retention/simulate?window=30d, POST /evidence/exports (body: tenant, start, end, scopes[]). Evidence export returns a signed URL to an S3/tenant-bucket with manifest and checksum. All APIs require scope 'retention:manage' and are audited in request logs.
ux_requirements: Console: new Derived Telemetry page under Compliance -> Retention. UX must show: 1) policy matrix (route/model/aggregation), 2) preview of expected retained series and storage estimate from simulator, 3) alias profile selector with 'preview alias' mode that shows pseudonymized sample rows, 4) evidence export wizard with redaction options and cost estimate. Accessibility: keyboard-navigable and follows existing Console patterns.
comments: 2025-02-14 — Aisha Patel: Initial draft accepted by Compliance. Raised concern about cross-backend alias consistency; asked infra to validate key rotation semantics.

2025-02-20 — Liam Chen: Spoke with ClickHouse infra team; they propose materialized column approach to store alias_key and provenance_hash. ENG outlined a perf impact estimate (~5% for writes under heavy load).

2025-02-25 — Kayla Morgan (Infra): Prototype PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/retention-service/pulls/467 — includes simulator endpoint and manifest schema v1. Feedback: need streaming-friendly exporter for >1TB ranges.
2025-03-01 — Legal (Samir Rao): Requested retention proof format include legal hold flags and chain-of-custody notes; added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-03 — Security (Priya Nair): Reviewed aliasing proposals; require HSM gating for reversible flows and audit hooks for key accesses. Assigned security review in tracker.
